title: Patient Reported Outcome Measures in Glaucoma Surgery
summary: The study prospectively investigates the impact of glaucoma surgical procedures on patients' health-related quality of life and subjective symptoms using validated Patient-Reported Outcome Measures (PROMs). While intraocular pressure is currently the primary outcome measure in many glaucoma studies, patient-centered endpoints are still rarely collected systematically. PROMs allow for a nuanced assessment of the subjective benefits of surgical interventions, especially when traditional clinical parameters show comparable results.

interventions.name: The study prospectively examines the impact of glaucoma surgical procedures on patients' health-related quality of life and subjective symptoms using validated Patient Reported Outcome Measures (PROMs).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients who are scheduled for a glaucoma surgical procedure (Istent Inject®, trabeculotomy using Trabectome or Kahook dual blade, 360° trabeculotomy following canaloplasty, ab interno canaloplasty, XEN implantation, trabeculectomy, and Ahmed valve or Paul implant), who are capable of giving consent and, after being informed, are willing to participate in the study.
Exclusion criteria:
- Persons under 18 years of age.  
- Persons who are mentally unable to complete the questionnaires for collecting the PROMs.
